mainTopic: When מלקות or מיתה cancels a payment, which תנא the קנס משנה follows, and a ברייתא about women who get no fine
overview: The גמרא finishes defending the source that someone liable for מלקות does not also pay. It does this by describing a case where he hit a person and tore his silk in the same act. רב חייא then asks how the תנא דבי חזקיה knows the פסוק about striking speaks of a weekday and not שבת. The גמרא proves it from the פסוק itself: the striker was warned, yet he still pays for the animal. Next, רב פפא asks אביי which תנא our משנה follows according to רבה, who says a קנס is paid even by someone who gets מיתה. רבי מאיר, רבי נחוניא בן הקנה and רבי יצחק each run into a problem. The גמרא concludes that רבה must hold like רבי יוחנן, who says that without a warning the man pays. רב מתנא then asks who argues with רבי נחוניא according to ריש לקיש, and the answer is רבי מאיר or רבי יצחק. Finally, a ברייתא lists women who get no fine at all. The גמרא begins asking what 'עריות' means there, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: But someone who gets lashes for hitting doesn't pay anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier source: a person who gets מלקות for hitting caused less than a פרוטה of damage, so he never owed money in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end, isn't he someone who is not subject to payment?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier proof that someone liable for מלקות does not pay. It points out that the case it used never involved money at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone gets מלקות for hitting a friend only when the damage is worth less than a פרוטה. In that case there is nothing to pay anyway. So how can we learn that מלקות cancels a payment that would otherwise be owed?

keyTerms.meaning: In the end, after all
Someone who is subject to paying money
Lashes, a physical punishment from the court

phrases.aramaic: סוֹף סוֹף לָאו בַּר תַּשְׁלוּמִין הוּא?
phrases.english: In the end, isn't he someone not subject to payment?
phrases.notes: He only gets lashes when the hit caused less than a פרוטה of damage, so there was nothing to pay anyway.

steps.triggerLanguage: סוֹף סוֹף לָאו בַּר תַּשְׁלוּמִין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation from the end of the previous discussion
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier proof that someone liable for מלקות is exempt from paying
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case of hitting with lashes involves damage under a פרוטה, so no payment was ever owed, and nothing can be learned about cancelling a payment

steps.title: He hit him and tore his silk at the same moment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where, at the moment of the hit, he also tore the victim's silk clothing, so a real payment is owed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where, at the same moment that he hit him, he tore his silk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by setting up a case where real money is owed at the same time as the lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing expensive silk creates a real money debt. Because it happens in the very same act as the hit that brings מלקות, we can now learn that the מלקות exempts him from that payment.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for, it applies to this case
At the same time as
Silk garments

phrases.english: It is only needed where, at the same time that he hit him,
he tore his silk garments.

steps.whatToRemember: The lashes and the money must come from one single act. Only then does the rule apply that he gets the lashes and does not pay.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case only involved a hit worth less than a פרוטה, so no payment existed
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is one where a single act also tore silk, so a real payment is cancelled by the מלקות

steps.title: Maybe the verse about striking is about שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא asks רבא how the תנא דבי חזקיה knows the פסוק comparing striking a person and an animal is about a weekday. Maybe it is about שבת, where even for an animal there is a difference between שוגג and מזיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא said to רבא: According to the תנא דבי חזקיה, who said the verse is about one who strikes a person and one who strikes an animal, how does he know it is written about a weekday, where there is no distinction? Perhaps it is written about שבת, where even for the animal itself there is a distinction.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא challenges the source of the תנא דבי חזקיה. He suggests the פסוק might be talking about שבת, which would ruin the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא דבי חזקיה learned that just as hitting an animal has no difference between שוגג and מזיד, the same is true for hitting a person, so even an accidental killer does not pay. But on שבת, hurting an animal on purpose brings מיתה for חילול שבת, so the מזיד would not pay while the שוגג would. If the פסוק is about שבת, then the animal case itself does have a difference, and the comparison falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא from the study hall of חזקיה
From where do we know?
To make a distinction
Perhaps
A weekday

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya said to Rava:
And according to the tanna of the school of Chizkiya,
who said "one who strikes a person" and "one who strikes an animal,"
from where do we know it is written about a weekday
and there is no distinction to make?
phrases.notes: No distinction between hurting an animal by accident or on purpose, since either way he simply pays.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is written about Shabbat,
where with the animal itself there is a distinction to make!
phrases.notes: On שבת, hurting it on purpose brings death for breaking שבת, so he wouldn't pay; by accident, he would.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב חִיָּיא לְרָבָא: וּלְתַנָּא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to a different source discussed earlier, the derivation of the תנא דבי חזקיה
steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא דבי חזקיה's comparison between striking an animal and striking a person
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the verse is about שבת, striking an animal does have a שוגג/מזיד difference, so it cannot teach that there is no difference for striking a person

steps.title: The verse must be about someone who was warned
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea and quotes the פסוק. Since the one who strikes a person gets death, he must have been warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: That should not enter your mind, as it is written: "And one who strikes an animal shall pay for it, and one who strikes a person shall be put to death." What is the case? If they did not warn him, why should one who strikes a person be put to death? Rather, it is obvious that they warned him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by reading the פסוק closely. First it shows that the person in this פסוק must have received a warning. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the one who strikes a person "shall be put to death." בית דין never gives מיתה without התראה (a warning). So the פסוק must be about a case where he was warned.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't think that, it can't be
What is the case? How does it look?
They warned him (התראה)
He shall be put to death

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind,
as it is written: "And one who strikes an animal shall pay for it,
and one who strikes a person shall be put to death."
What is the case?
If they did not warn him,
why should one who strikes a person be put to death?
Rather, it is obvious that they warned him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Proving the scenario from the wording of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse might be about striking an animal on שבת
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse speaks of someone who was warned, which leads to the conclusion in the next step

steps.title: So the verse must be about a weekday
steps.stepSummary: If he was warned and it was שבת, he would get מיתה for the animal too and would not pay. Since the פסוק says he pays for the animal, it must be a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is on שבת, would one who strikes an animal pay for it?! Rather, is it not about a weekday?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer. A warned person on שבת would not pay for the animal, so the פסוק must be about a weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we just showed he was warned, if it were שבת then hurting the animal would bring מיתה for חילול שבת, and he would be exempt from paying. But the פסוק says "he shall pay for it." So it must be a weekday, and the proof of the תנא דבי חזקיה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He shall pay for it
Rather, is it not so that...

phrases.english: And if it is on Shabbat,
would one who strikes an animal pay for it?!
Rather, is it not about a weekday?

steps.whatToRemember: Because the person was warned and still pays for the animal, the פסוק must be about a weekday. So the תנא דבי חזקיה's comparison holds: for striking a person, too, there is no difference between שוגג and מזיד.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 4
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The verse is about a weekday, so the תנא דבי חזקיה's derivation stands

steps.title: According to רבה, whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks אביי: רבה holds that קנס is a special Torah rule, paid even by someone who gets מיתה. So which תנא does our משנה follow?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: According to רבה, who said it is a novelty that the Torah introduced with fines, and even though he is executed he pays, whose opinion does he say the משנה follows?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא opens a new question about רבה's view. This step sets up the next steps, which test each possible תנא one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that a קנס is special: a person pays it even if he also gets מיתה. Our משנה lists which forbidden girls get a קנס and which don't. רב פפא wants to know which תנא's view could fit both רבה's rule and the משנה's list.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine, a set Torah payment that is not based on actual damage
A novelty, a special rule that does not follow normal logic
He is executed
Our משנה
According to whom?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
According to Rabba, who said:
It is a novelty that the Torah introduced with fines,
and even though he is executed, he pays,
whose opinion does he say the Mishnah follows?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: לְרַבָּה דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about רבה's view of קנס
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא our משנה follows, according to רבה's view that a קנס is paid even by someone who gets מיתה

steps.title: רבי מאיר doesn't fit: the daughter case
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה follows רבי מאיר, then according to רבה even someone who gets מיתה pays the קנס. So why does the משנה exempt him for his daughter?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי מאיר, his daughter is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, רבי מאיר, and shows it doesn't fit the משנה's ruling about a daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבה, רבי מאיר holds that even someone who gets מיתה pays the קנס. Relations with a daughter bring מיתה, yet the משנה says he does not pay. So the משנה cannot follow רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult, there is a problem
His daughter

phrases.english: If it follows Rabbi Meir,
his daughter is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to רב פפא's question
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing the משנה according to רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבה, רבי מאיר says even someone who gets מיתה pays the קנס, but the משנה exempts the daughter case, which carries מיתה

steps.title: רבי נחוניא doesn't fit: the sister case
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה treats כרת like מיתה and exempts from payment. So why does the משנה make him pay the קנס for his sister?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, his sister is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option, רבי נחוניא בן הקנה, and shows it doesn't fit the משנה's ruling about a sister.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה holds that people liable for כרת are exempt from payment, just like people liable for מיתה. Relations with a sister bring כרת, yet the משנה says he pays the קנס. So the משנה cannot follow him either.

keyTerms.meaning: His sister
Being cut off, a punishment from Heaven

phrases.english: If it follows Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana,
his sister is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כְּרַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנָה, קַשְׁיָא אֲחוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible answer after רבי מאיר failed
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing the משנה according to רבי נחוניא בן הקנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He exempts people liable for כרת from payment, but the משנה obligates the קנס for a sister, which carries כרת

steps.title: רבי יצחק doesn't fit: the ממזרת case
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says כרת brings no מלקות, so he pays. But someone who gets מלקות does not pay. So why does the משנה make him pay for a ממזרת, which brings מלקות?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it follows רבי יצחק, a ממזרת is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the third option, רבי יצחק, and shows it also runs into a problem, this time with a ממזרת. All three options have now failed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק holds that people liable for כרת do not get מלקות, so they pay the קנס. But someone who does get מלקות is exempt from paying. Relations with a ממזרת bring מלקות, yet the משנה says he pays, so this option fails too.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl born from a forbidden relationship; marrying her is a לאו that brings מלקות
A Torah prohibition, usually punished with מלקות

phrases.english: If it follows Rabbi Yitzchak,
a mamzeret is difficult!

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבה, none of the three תנאים fits the משנה at first: רבי מאיר fails on the daughter, רבי נחוניא on the sister, and רבי יצחק on the ממזרת. The next steps show how רבה can still explain the משנה, by holding like רבי יוחנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Each problem comes from a different case in the משנה. Match each תנא to his own case: daughter = מיתה, sister = כרת, ממזרת = מלקות.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the third and last possible answer
steps.kashyaTarget: Placing the משנה according to רבי יצחק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He exempts anyone who gets מלקות from paying, but the משנה obligates the קנס for a ממזרת, which brings מלקות

steps.title: רבה's answer works only if he holds like רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to resolve רב פפא's question. If רבה holds like רבי יוחנן, he can explain the משנה the same way רבי יוחנן does, as a case with no warning, so the man pays. But if he holds like ריש לקיש, how can he explain it?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is fine if he holds like רבי יוחנן, because then he can also explain the משנה like רבי יוחנן. But if he holds like ריש לקיש, how does he explain it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא responds to רב פפא's three difficulties by offering רבה a way out if he follows רבי יוחנן. It then asks what he could say if he follows ריש לקיש, and the next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says that if there was no warning (התראה), the man pays, even for a sin that brings מלקות. ריש לקיש says a sin that brings מלקות exempts him from paying even with no warning. If רבה holds like ריש לקיש, the 'no warning' answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one side)
An אמורא. Without a warning, the man pays even for a sin that brings מלקות
An אמורא. A sin that brings מלקות exempts payment even without a warning
Explains, answers

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two אמוראים. For רבי יוחנן, the missing warning is what makes him pay. For ריש לקיש, the missing warning does not help at all.

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן —
phrases.english: This works out well if he holds like Rabbi Yochanan —
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבה, whose view the גמרא has been testing against our משנה.

phrases.aramaic: הוּא נָמֵי מְתָרֵץ לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן.
phrases.english: he can also explain it like Rabbi Yochanan.
But if he holds like Reish Lakish,
how does he explain it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the three difficulties of steps 7-9. It offers רבי יוחנן's 'no warning' explanation for רבה, and questions what he would do if he follows ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: Resolving רב פפא's difficulty for רבה if רבה holds like ריש לקיש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבה holds like ריש לקיש, a sin that brings מלקות exempts from paying even without a warning. So the 'no warning' answer cannot explain why the משנה obligates payment.

steps.title: רבה must hold like רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבה is forced to hold like רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: You have no choice but to say that he holds like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question. Since the answer only works with רבי יוחנן, רבה must agree with רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not try to fit ריש לקיש's view in. Instead it draws a conclusion about what רבה holds: without a warning, a man pays even for a sin that brings מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: You are forced to say, by necessity
He holds (this view)

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's way of explaining the משנה only works if he holds like רבי יוחנן: without a warning, the man pays even for a sin that brings מלקות.

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּרְחָךְ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: Perforce, he holds like Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כׇּרְחָךְ כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 by concluding which view רבה must hold.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Forced conclusion about the speaker's underlying view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe רבה could hold like ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה must hold like רבי יוחנן, so the 'no warning' explanation stands.

steps.title: Which תנא argues with רבי נחוניא according to ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנא asks אביי: according to ריש לקיש, who treats מלקות like מיתה, which תנא disagrees with רבי נחוניא בן הקנה and makes the man pay?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנא said to אביי: According to ריש לקיש, who said the Torah clearly treats people who get מלקות like people who get מיתה, which תנא disagrees with רבי נחוניא בן הקנה?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רב מתנא wants to know which תנא could be behind our משנה's ruling that a man pays for his sister, if we follow ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחוניא בן הקנה exempts from payment anyone who gets כרת. Our משנה makes the man pay for his sister, which is a כרת sin, so its author must disagree with רבי נחוניא. But for ריש לקיש, the מלקות for that sin should also exempt him. So who is that author?

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who asks the question to אביי
The Torah explicitly included
Those liable to receive lashes
Those liable to the death penalty
Who disagrees with him

phrases.english: Rav Mattana said to Abaye,
According to Reish Lakish, who said:
The Torah explicitly included
those liable to lashes like those liable to death,
phrases.notes: He means that, just like someone who gets מיתה, someone who gets מלקות does not pay.

phrases.english: who is the tanna who disagrees
with Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKana?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבה's view to the same question asked according to ריש לקיש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא, according to ריש לקיש, obligates payment against רבי נחוניא בן הקנה

steps.title: Either רבי מאיר or רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it is either רבי מאיר or רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Either רבי מאיר or רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב מתנא's question with two possible תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that someone who gets מלקות still pays the קנס, so מלקות does not exempt him. רבי יצחק holds that כרת sins bring no מלקות at all, so nothing exempts him. Either way the man pays, unlike the view of רבי נחוניא.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא. One who gets מלקות still pays the קנס
A תנא. כרת sins do not bring מלקות

steps.whatToRemember: Even for ריש לקיש, our משנה can follow רבי מאיר or רבי יצחק. Each has his own reason why the man still pays.

phrases.english: Either Rabbi Meir,
or Rabbi Yitzchak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר, אִי רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר (מלקות does not stop the קנס) or רבי יצחק (כרת sins bring no מלקות).

steps.title: A ברייתא lists girls who get no fine at all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that עריות, שניות לעריות, a ממאנת, an איילונית, and a woman sent away for a bad reputation get neither קנס nor פיתוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: forbidden relatives and secondary forbidden relatives get neither a rape fine nor a seduction fine. A girl who refused her marriage gets neither. An איילונית gets neither. A woman who leaves because of a bad name gets neither.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. It lists women for whom no fine is paid, whether for rape or for seduction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has its own reason. A ממאנת was already married, so she is no longer presumed a virgin. An איילונית never reaches the stage of a נערה. The case of עריות seems to clash with our משנה, which does make the man pay for some forbidden relatives, so the גמרא will next ask what this means.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (opens a ברייתא)
Forbidden relationships
Secondary forbidden relatives (forbidden by the רבנן)
Seduction, and the fine paid for it
A girl who refuses (leaves) a marriage made while she was a minor
A woman who never develops into a נערה

steps.mimraCoreRuling: עריות, שניות לעריות, a ממאנת, an איילונית, and a woman who leaves due to a bad reputation get neither קנס nor פיתוי.

steps.title: What do the ברייתא's terms mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'עריות' and 'שניות לעריות' mean in the ברייתא, and begins to suggest an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'forbidden relatives,' and what is meant by 'secondary forbidden relatives'? If you say 'forbidden relatives' means...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the ברייתא's first two terms. It is setting up its first suggestion, which continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא needs these terms defined because our משנה does make the man pay for some forbidden relatives, such as a sister. The word 'אילימא' tells us a first suggestion is coming, which the גמרא will probably reject.
